convention: RESOLVED: the FAO 1952 "population" series is FIVE DISTINCT INDICATORS sharing one item code (r_fao_population_1952_10_18): "population total", "population agricultural", "population agricultural ocupati[on]" (economically active in agriculture) and its male/female splits. Layer B keeps them apart in the `indicator` column; the item code does not, so any median keyed on `item` alone MIXES all five and lands somewhere between them. "population total" IS true total population and can be used as such. A figure around a third of the total is the agricultural-occupied indicator, NOT a defect and NOT evidence of a territorial mismatch. Always read `indicator` before using a figure. Separately, 21 of the 212 entities carrying a total-population row have an implausible 1937->1951 step (extraction defects: Afghanistan 1951 = 0, Pakistan 1951 = 5,842k against 66,009k in 1937, Austria 1951 = 916k), so check per-entity plausibility.
evidence: Measured 2026-08-14 against consolidated_layer_b.parquet (868 fao1952 population rows, years 1937 and 1951). Yugoslavia 1937: total 15,722k (1931 census 13.9M, 1948 census 15.77M), agricultural 10,629k, agricultural-occupied 5,083k -- the previously recorded "median ~5.08M" is EXACTLY the agricultural-occupied row, and also the median of the five indicator-mixed 1937 rows the evidence bundle saw. Turkey: total 16,823k (1937) and 20,935k (1951), matching the 1935 and 1950 censuses; the recorded "~6,086k" is exactly the median of Turkey's ten indicator-mixed rows, (5,712+6,459)/2 = 6,085.5. Saar 1937 = 821k is the "population total" indicator under country label "Saar"; the Saar's agricultural rows sit under a SEPARATE label "France  Saar", so that bundle only ever saw the total series -- there was never a contradiction, and the "small/non-agricultural territory" hypothesis is falsified. The claimed uniform ~1/3 cross-check also fails: agricultural-occupied/total in 1937 is USA 6.5%, Germany 12.4%, Japan 20.2%, and the source carries NO USSR population row at all (its aggregate is literally labelled "GENERAL TOTAL EXCLUDING THE USSR"). Independent check of the total series, 1937: Italy 42,372k, France 41,200k, Egypt 16,008k, India 304,333k, China 452,460k, Poland 31,600k, USA 128,961k -- all within a few percent of accepted figures; 191 of 212 entities show a plausible 1951/1937 ratio.
verified_by: issue-13 re-measurement (indicator column resolves the apparent contradiction)
retest: 2026-08-17 re-measured (11_retest_conventions.py): 868 fao1952 population rows, years 1937 and 1951, FIVE distinct `indicator` values under ONE item_code; Yugoslavia 1937 'population total' 15,722k, agricultural 10,629k, agricultural-occupied 5,083k; Turkey total 16,823k (1937) / 20,935k (1951); Saar total 821k with its agricultural rows still under the separate label 'France  Saar'. Every figure in the evidence column reproduced exactly. Conclusion stands.

convention: juan reports Finland on the settled post-1940 reduced-territory basis throughout 1941-1960 — it does NOT switch to the briefly recaptured Karelia borders during the Continuation War.
evidence: Sown-area series (barley/oats/wheat) smooth and continuous across 1941-1944 and the 1944 armistice; oats fall 472k ha (1939) to a 310k ha trough (1945) then recover — wartime disruption, not a territorial step.
retest: 2026-08-17 re-measured: oats sown area 1939=472,000 ha falling monotonically to a 1945 trough of 310,000 ha (1940 427k, 1941 399k, 1942 379k, 1943 354k, 1944 314k), then 437,000 ha by 1950; no year-on-year step above 15% anywhere in 1939-1945, so no territorial switch at either the 1940 cession or the 1944 armistice. Reproduced exactly. Conclusion stands.

convention: IIA figures reported under 'Djibouti'/French Somaliland for coffee, green are transit/re-export volumes of Ethiopian-origin coffee passing through the port via the Djibouti-Addis Ababa railway, not domestic production of the territory.
evidence: Web research: the Djibouti-Addis Ababa railway (1897-1917) made Djibouti the premier export port for Ethiopian coffee from the Harar region; France held a near-monopoly on Ethiopia's export trade via this route until the mid-1950s. Magnitude (median 14,114 t/yr) is implausible as domestic output for a small arid territory with no known coffee agriculture.
retest: 2026-08-17 re-measured: 'coffee, green' under 'djibouti' is 5 rows, years 1930-1933, median 14,113.7 t (min 12,514 t, max 21,106 t). The median reproduced exactly; the observed span is 1930-1933, narrower than the 1929-1945 window named in verified_by, so the flag is written on (source, label, item) with no year bound. Conclusion stands.

convention: IIA/agricultural yearbooks report Algeria as its own territorial reporting unit, distinct from metropolitan France, despite Algeria's administrative integration into France during the colonial period -- unlike some empire-vs-metropole ambiguities (e.g. Austria/Cisleithania), there is no fold-up risk for this label.
evidence: Staple magnitudes (olives, oranges, cotton) match Algeria's own Mediterranean-belt agricultural geography rather than combined France+Algeria totals, and IIA consistently tabulates Algeria separately across the observed span with no discontinuity at years when metropolitan-France reporting conventions might otherwise intrude. || Corroborated by an independent re-measurement, not a second opinion on the same evidence: data/final/source_stated_area_basis.csv records IIA stating an ALGERIE area in six editions (1909;1925;1929;1932;1933;1938), 2,195,696 km2 against our 2,318,386 km2 colony polygon, ratio 1.056, flagged `agrees`. A source folding Algeria into France would not state a separate area for it six times. Re-tested structurally by check_iia_algeria: iia carries 567 algeria rows against 426 france rows as separate labels, 20 shared items.

convention: In fao1952, the plain country label 'France' denotes metropolitan France only. Algeria and the Saar (including the 1948-56 France-Saar customs union) are reported under separate distinct labels ('Algeria', 'French North Africa Algeria', 'Saar', 'France Saar'), not folded into 'France'.
evidence: fao1952 carries France (324 rows), Algeria (263) and Saar (146) as separate labels, and ALSO carries a distinct 'France Saar' combination (131 rows) for the 1948-56 customs union -- a source folding the union into 'France' would not tabulate the combination separately. 47 items shared between France and Algeria, Algeria's median below France's in 35.

convention: Mitchell's colonial-Algeria agricultural series (crop areas in ha, production in tonnes) follow the same civil-departments reporting basis already documented for IIA under issue 166: they cover northern Algeria (the departments of Alger, Oran, Constantine, ~575,511 km2) rather than the full colony polygon including the Sahara Southern Territories annexed in 1902 (~2.44M km2). Tell: cropland magnitudes (wheat ~1.3M ha, barley ~1.15M ha) are agronomically plausible only for the northern departments, never the Sahara.
evidence: CAMEL TEST, independent of the cropland magnitudes this was learned from: camels are a Saharan animal, so a widening to the full colony at the 1902 Southern Territories annexation would step the herd up. Measured across a 74-year series from 1867: 203,000 head median pre-1902 vs 180,500 from 1902, 0.89x -- it goes slightly DOWN. Cropland cannot discriminate (desert holds little either way). Cross-source second line: Mitchell and IIA agree on shared items (oats 164,000 vs 185,000 ha, 0.89; olive oil 22,000 vs 20,685 t, 1.06) and IIA's civil-departments basis is issue 166's.

convention: IIA's 'Netherlands' label denotes metropolitan (European) Netherlands only, excluding the Netherlands East Indies and other Dutch colonies, which IIA reports under separate colonial labels.
evidence: AGRONOMIC and concurrent: ZERO tropical items under `netherlands` against four under `indonesia` (cacao beans, coffee green, rubber natural, tea) across 33 SHARED years, 203 vs 378 rows. The Netherlands cannot grow any of them and the East Indies was a major producer of all four, so a folded-in colony would put them under the metropolitan label. Independently, state/iia_label_provenance.csv measures `netherlands` as territory_signal=clean, 95% its own raw label, with the Dutch colonies carried as separate raw labels (dutch east indies, dutch guiana, dutch new guinea, dutch curacao).

convention: IIA yearbook 'Austria' entries through 1917/1918 report Cisleithania (the Austrian half of Austria-Hungary, ~300,560 km2 including Bohemia, Moravia, Galicia, etc.), not rump/modern Austria — consistent with the Mitchell ISH convention already documented for this polity.
evidence: TEMPORAL STEP at the 1918 dissolution, independent of the magnitude-plausibility argument this was learned from: median pre-1918 vs 1920+ ratios are sugar raw centrifugal 938,389 -> 128,900 t (0.14), phosphate 323,050 -> 36,327 (0.11), hemp yarn 3,336 -> 352 (0.11), wine 310,305 -> 85,075 (0.27). Steeper than the 3.6x area ratio because Bohemia and Moravia were the empire's sugar-beet heartland and both left in 1918. A label meaning rump Austria throughout would show no step. CAVEAT: the label also draws ~12% of its values from raw `austria-hungary` (the whole monarchy) concurrently, which is why austria|iia|1909-1917 is quarantined rather than banked -- this establishes what the dominant 73% means.

convention: In the IIA raw extract, the plain label 'libya' is the whole-Libya (Tripolitania+Cyrenaica+Fezzan) aggregate; sub-provincial data is carried under distinct sibling raw labels 'libya: tripolitania' and 'libya: cyrenaica'. convention: Mitchell (International Historical Statistics) reports Syria's agricultural series as a standalone geographic unit continuously through the 1958-1961 United Arab Republic union period, not merged with Egypt's figures.
evidence: CONCURRENCY plus AREA, both independent of the continuity argument this was learned from. Mitchell carries `egypt` (1,187 rows) as its own label in every union year 1958-1960 alongside `syrian arab republic` (296 rows), so Egypt's figures are not inside Syria's. And Syrian wheat AREA is flat across the union's start -- 1,495k ha (1957), 1,460k (1958), 1,422k (1959), 1,550k (1960) -- where folding in Egypt's ~600k ha would step it ~1.4x. Production tonnage is unusable for this: Syrian wheat output swings 438k -> 1,051k -> 1,354k -> 562k over 1955-1958, harvest variance that would drown any territorial signal.
